page: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a member of the storage-optimized instance family designed for sequential, high-capacity disk access. Built on the x86_64 architecture using the Xen hypervisor, it is powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 32 GB, translating to 4 GB per core, backed by a 45 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets.

The primary differentiator for this hardware configuration is its bundled local storage, featuring a direct-attached 2000 GB HDD. It operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not bundle any GPU accelerators, emphasizing disk capacity and compute balance over parallel vector processing.

Synthetic benchmark assessments reveal modest compute capabilities consistent with its processor generation. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 904.0 and a multi-core score of 3371.0, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 6218.11 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 4177.44. While uncached large-block memory bandwidth reaches 38.02 GB/sec for reads and 22.65 GB/sec for writes, transactional database throughput and latency-sensitive tasks are constrained, recording 2.51 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance offers cost-effective mass storage density by relying on magnetic disk media rather than flash memory. The tradeoff is lower IOPS and modest CPU throughput compared to modern NVMe-backed configurations. Consequently, this server is suitable for batch processing, log ingestion, distributed storage nodes, and sequential ETL data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor and driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. It offers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 32 GB of memory to maintain a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. A distinct feature of this server is its bundled 2000 GB local HDD, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include a GPU. Benchmark testing places its computational throughput in lower relative tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3371.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6218.11, while memory bandwidth remains steady at 38.02 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. By bundling high-capacity rotational media, the server prioritizes storage volume over processing speed, making it suitable for distributed file systems, sequential data warehousing, batch pipelines, and log collection.
